s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive radicular pain and neuropathic symptoms in the lower extremity
salient_findings: Radicular pain radiating from lower back down the left leg
Mild hypesthesia in the left L5–S1 dermatome
Cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone
key_facts: 8-month history of radicular pain
Pain radiates from lower back down the left leg
Occasional tingling
No weakness or autonomic symptoms
No history of trauma or injury
Mild hypesthesia in the left L5–S1 dermatome
Normal muscle strength
Negative Lasègue, Kernig, Bragard, and Sicard signs
Electromyography shows neuropathic irritation of the left L4, L5, S1, and S2 roots
Lumbosacral MRI shows a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone
Mass measures approximately 13.9 cm in length and 1.9 cm in maximal diameter
Mass is hypointense on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's MRI shows a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone, which is consistent with a schwannoma, a type of nerve sheath tumor.

shortlist.label: Neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are also consistent with a neurofibroma, another type of nerve sheath tumor.

shortlist.label: Tarlov cyst
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's MRI shows a cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone, which could be consistent with a Tarlov cyst, a type of spinal nerve root cyst.

shortlist.label: Plexiform neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, the patient's symptoms and imaging findings could also be consistent with a plexiform neurofibroma, a type of nerve sheath tumor that can cause nerve root irritation.

shortlist.label: Intraneural ganglion cyst
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's MRI shows a cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone, which could be consistent with an intraneural ganglion cyst, a rare type of cyst that can cause nerve root irritation.

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of radicular pain and tingling, along with the MRI findings of a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone that is hypointense on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images, is most consistent with an intraneural ganglion cyst. The lack of attachment to pelvic organs and the mass arising from the sciatic nerve also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: Schwannomas are typically solid tumors, not completely cystic

rejected.label: Neurofibroma
rejected.why: Neurofibromas are also typically solid and may be associated with neurofibromatosis type 1

rejected.label: Tarlov cyst
rejected.why: Tarlov cysts are typically found in the spinal canal and are associated with the nerve roots, not extending along the course of the sciatic nerve

rejected.label: Plexiform neurofibroma
rejected.why: Plexiform neurofibromas are complex, multinodular tumors that are typically associated with neurofibromatosis type 1 and do not match the description of a solitary, cystic mass
